title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: Hold: the package-availability API entry names body properties but supplies neither their values nor a usable JSON body. The roadmap facts and documented navigation paths are supported, but the advice about a skill's data reach also assumes a boundary Microsoft has not established for the catalog.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Copilot Studio catalog through which makers discover and reuse skills instead of rebuilding instructions and workflows for each agent.
claims.quote: With the Skills catalog in Copilot Studio, makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the catalog's skills as approved organisational skills that makers can selectively share.
claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.claim: The roadmap says Microsoft 365 App Store powers the shared catalog.
claims.quote: The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store

claims.claim: The roadmap plans shared skills that extend across Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.
claims.quote: enables shared skills to extend across experiences such as Copilot Studio M365 copilot, and Cowork

claims.claim: The roadmap describes centralised governance for the shared catalog.
claims.quote: helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance.

claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" license roles default rollout. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview, skills-add-existing; read whats-new excerpts describing marketplace-shared skills without identifying them as the roadmap's catalog.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: The Browse skills and sharing flows are preview documentation subject to change.
claims.quote:
Browse and add shared skills (preview)

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A maker adds a shared skill through the agent's Build tab, the + icon next to Skills, Browse skills (preview), a skill's details and Add.
claims.quote:
Select the Build tab.
Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview).
Browse the shared skills available to you.
Select the skill you want to add.
On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.claim: The skills available in Browse skills are those shared with the maker by admins or skill owners.
claims.quote: You can browse and add skills that other people shared with you to your agent. The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A skill has a name, description and instructions that guide the agent's behaviour for particular tasks.
claims.quote: A skill is a capability defined by a name, a description, and instructions that tell the agent how to handle specific types of tasks or scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding a shared skill creates a snapshot in the agent while retaining a reference to the original.
claims.quote: When you add a shared skill, the agent gets a snapshot of the skill while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Makers receive an update notification when they open an agent using an older shared-skill version.
claims.quote: You receive a skill update notification when you open an agent that uses an older version of a shared skill.

claims.claim: Makers can choose to update an added shared skill.
claims.quote: You can choose to update to the new version by selecting the update button for the skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: A creator can keep a skill private with Only you or share it with Specific users or groups in your organization.
claims.quote:
Only you: Keeps the skill private to your account.
Specific users or groups in your organization: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address. People and groups you add can use the skill.

claims.claim: A skill package can contain supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.claim: Recipients of a shared skill can add it to their agents.
claims.quote: The people and groups you share with can then add the skill to their agents.

claims.claim: The orchestration runtime activates skills based on the user's message and the skill description rather than requiring the user to request a skill by name.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct an agent to use a particular tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An owner must share an edited skill again to make its latest version available to previous recipients.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an additional approval step for a maker adding a shared skill beyond selecting Add.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles approval. Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; the former ends adding at Add, while the latter's approvals concern plugins and MCP registrations, not this catalog flow.

claims.claim: The feature documentation does not specify what data a catalog skill can reach.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skill" "data access" "instructions"; Copilot Studio "Browse skills" harness admin sharing policy permissions data access. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing; no catalog-specific data-reach specification appeared.

claims.claim: Readers can treat a catalog skill's data reach as determined by the agent that adds it.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skill" "data access" "instructions"; Copilot Studio "Browse skills" harness admin sharing policy permissions data access. Read skills-overview and skills-manage: neither establishes this data-access mechanism for catalog skills.
claims.fix: Replace 'Treat reach as set by the agent that adds the skill, and confirm this once Microsoft documents the catalog.' with 'Confirm the skill's data-access boundaries before using it with organisational data.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents no tenant-level switch specifically for the maker's skill-sharing control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles approval. Read skills-manage, admin-sharing-controls-limits and skills-copilot-studio-rule; none specifies a switch for this maker skill-sharing action.

claims.claim: Roles required for the named catalog are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" license roles default rollout; Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles approval. Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; neither assigns an administrative role to the named catalog.

claims.claim: The cited plugins-and-skills management page names AI Administrator and Global Administrator for MCP registration review and consent, not as the roles for skill management.
claims.quote:
To complete the review and approval process, you must meet two requirements:
You must have access to the Tools page ...
You must be able to grant tenant-wide consent.
Two roles meet both requirements:
AI Administrator.
Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The skills overview describes Generative and Topic skills for the Customer Conversation harness.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: Generative skills ... and Topic skills, which are deterministic, authored flows of steps and conditions

claims.claim: The shared-skill instructions do not explicitly enumerate the harnesses supported by Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" harness admin sharing policy permissions data access. Read skills-manage and skills-overview; the former's Browse section gives no supported-harness list and the latter lists Browse separately from the harness-specific creation methods.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence specific to the named skills catalog is published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog license pricing Copilot Credits skills billing rate; "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" license roles default rollout. Read skills-manage, billing-credit-overview and billing-licensing excerpts; no catalog-specific licence is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate rate for browsing, adding or sharing a skill is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog license pricing Copilot Credits skills billing rate. Read skills-manage, billing-credit-overview and requirements-messages-management excerpts; no separate browsing, adding or sharing rate found.

claims.claim: The credit cost of an agent using an added skill is not stated.
claims.quote: The number of Copilot Credits these experiences consume depends on how they are designed, how often they run, and the features they use.
claims.fix: Replace 'The credit cost of an agent that uses an added skill is not stated either.' with 'No catalog-specific credit rate is published; agents using shared skills remain subject to their documented harness billing.' The current wording obscures the general billing rule already stated on the page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot harness uses usage-based billing in Copilot Credits, including building, testing, evaluation and use.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts when a maker starts building.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Consumption is the documented licensing model for the harness-backed shared-skill experience described, while catalog-specific licensing remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure.

claims.claim: Variable cost is consistent with the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Package user availability is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Tools > Plugins.
Select the plugin that you want to manage.
Open Users ...
Managing a skill uses the same actions and steps as managing a plugin, so this section applies to both plugins and skills.

claims.claim: The printed PATCH entry supplies a usable request for setting package availability to selected users and groups.
claims.quote:
In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a copilotPackageDetail object.
"allowedUsersAndGroups": [ { "resourceType": "user", "resourceId": "5d9fa31e-626e-45fb-b6e7-d8f1f11933a9" }
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api.call and its rendered copy with: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} with JSON body {"availableTo":"allowedForSome","allowedUsersAndGroups":[{"resourceType":"user","resourceId":"<user-id>"},{"resourceType":"group","resourceId":"<group-id>"}]}. The endpoint and property names are correct, but merely naming body properties gives neither the required availability value nor the access-entity structure.

claims.claim: A standalone skill package can be blocked through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Tools > Plugins.
From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block.
Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry lists plugin and separately packaged skill records.
claims.quote: Use Agents > Tools > Registry to review plugin and separately packaged skill records in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=elementTypes/any(e:e eq 'AgentSkills') inventories packages containing skills.
claims.quote:
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages
To filter by element type, use the any lambda operator on the elementTypes collection ...
AgentSkills | Titles that contain skills.

claims.claim: The maker sharing dialog is reached through Build > skill > … > Share > Share.
claims.quote:
Select the skill you want to share to open the skill configuration panel.
Select the three dots (…) and then select Share.
On the details page, select Share in the upper-right corner.

claims.claim: No API is documented as the equivalent of this preview maker-side skill-sharing action.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skills sharing API Dataverse botcomponent Power Platform API pac PowerShell. Read skills-manage, botcomponent Web API, GrantAccess excerpts and pac copilot (searched skill/share); no equivalent action is identified.

claims.where: controls[0..2].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that the general Microsoft 365 package controls govern the named Copilot Studio skills catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills" "share" "API" "catalog"; Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles approval. Read skills-manage, package API overview, administrator-guide and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; no explicit catalog linkage found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0..1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: General Microsoft 365 package controls can scope a standalone skill package to users and groups or block access to the package.
claims.quote:
Manage user availability | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. | Make the package available to all users, no users, or specific users and groups.
Block ... Prevent users and agents from accessing the package.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A bundled skill has no individual blocking control; the containing plugin's controls apply.
claims.quote: For a bundled skill, apply the plugin's controls. You can't block an individual skill inside a package today.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have controls separate from the Microsoft 365 package controls.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: Some skills, including those used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, are stored in OneDrive rather than the plugin registry.
claims.quote: Don't assume every skill is stored in the plugin registry. Skills used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive today.

claims.claim: The publisher-category control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access offers publisher categories Microsoft, your organization and certified external publishers for plugin access.
claims.quote: Under the installation settings, choose which publisher categories users can access: Microsoft, your organization, or certified external publishers.

claims.claim: The Package Management API's update and block operations are preview.
claims.quote:
Update package (preview) | PATCH /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}
Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: An agent's Copilot Credit consumption can be viewed on its Monitor page in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: You can view the total Copilot credits an agent consumes on its Monitor page in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The documented capability is maker-opt-in: a maker chooses to add a shared skill, and no catalog-enablement switch was found.
claims.quote:
You can browse and add skills that other people shared with you to your agent.
Select the skill you want to add.
On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the named catalog's arrival mechanics, a required administrative action or a switch specifically disabling Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" "Browse skills" admin disable sharing roles approval. Read skills-manage, skills-copilot-studio-rule and agent-settings excerpts; no catalog arrival requirement or Browse skills switch found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls

Track Copilot Credit consumption for agents that use added skills in the Monitor page ...
The controls table contains only user availability, package blocking, package inventory and maker sharing.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet beginning 'Track Copilot Credit consumption' so the checklist names only controls represented in the existing table.
